text:
leah: quick RFC gist — proposing ergonomic changes to the Go Generator streaming API after hitting multiple friction points while onboarding teams. TL;DR: return a stream object with Next()/Close()/Context() instead of a plain receive-only channel so callers have explicit ownership and can cancel handshakes, drain, and handle auth refresh races.

leah: current pain: callers expect ctx cancel to be enough, but when background auth refresh / reconnects happen the runtime can spawn internal handshakes that don't observe the original cancel (and we have no explicit handle to force-terminate them). leads to confusing hanging goroutines for sampleapps and users.

omar: can you sketch the proposed surface? i remember earlier we avoided objects to keep API simple.

leah: sure — minimal proposal:
```go
type Stream struct {
  // Next blocks and returns the next token; io.EOF when complete.
  Next(ctx context.Context) (Token, error)
  // Close stops the stream immediately and releases resources.
  Close() error
  // Ctx returns the internal context tied to the stream's lifetime
  // (useful for derived handshakes). callers shouldn't cancel this ctx.
  Ctx() context.Context
}

// usage (recommended)
ctx := context.Background()
stream := client.Generator("gpt-small").Stream(ctx, Prompt("hello"))
defer stream.Close() // important for early exits
for {
  tok, err := stream.Next(ctx)
  if err == io.EOF { break }
  if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
  fmt.Print(tok.Text)
}
```

kevin: that makes sense. Close() solves many caller-side ownership problems and reduces reliance on callers wiring cancel semantics correctly. the Ctx() idea is interesting — runtime can derive per-handshake contexts from stream.Ctx() and cancel them when Close() is called.

sofia: +1 for Close(). Two UX notes: (1) keep a convenience helper that returns a channel for people who prefer range-style loops (compat shim), and (2) we should make Close idempotent and safe to call multiple times from different goroutines.

emily: from DX/sampleapps POV: we should publish a small migration note and update the Go quickstart to always defer Close(). many examples currently assume ctx cancellation only which users copy-paste. also add a short snippet around auth rotation: show how to coordinate token refresh with stream lifecycle (avoid calling client.AuthRefresh while stream is mid-handshake).

omar: what's the compatibility plan? we can't break existing callers.

leah: plan: (1) add the Stream object as a new API while keeping the channel-based Stream(...) as a thin shim that returns a channel backed by the object for a release cycle, (2) instrument runtime to detect leaked handshakes and emit a metric, and (3) deprecate the channel shim after one major release with migration docs.

kevin: tests? we need a deterministic unit that simulates token rotation + mid-handshake cancel. also stress test for concurrency: Close racing with Next/Resume.

leah: agreed. I'll add three tests: handshake-cancel-assert-no-goroutine-growth, close-idempotent-race, and channel-shim-parity. I'll also add an example in go-sampleapps showing a real auth-rotation loop plus proper Close() usage.

sofia: ops/support request: could we also add an internal debug endpoint or metric that exposes per-client active streams and last handshake state? when customers file "hang" tickets support can point to that.

omar: metrics sound good and low-risk. add an internal debug handler guarded behind an env flag. don't expose on public control plane.

emily: small docs nit: update generator README to mention Resume() semantics (i.e., if you spawn background goroutines that expect the stream to finish, they should listen for stream.Ctx() or check Close()). write example for Resume pattern showing use of a WaitGroup and Close().

leah: noted. i'll draft the PR with the shim, tests, and docs. assigning to @kevin for runtime review and @omar for API review. will reference related issues in the PR.

ci-bot: created draft PR leah/stream-api-object (WIP) — build queued

kevin: thanks — i'll take a look today. one implementation note: make the internal transport manager select on both the per-handshake ctx and a close channel to guarantee teardown even if a handshake goroutine hasn't observed token change events.

sofia: +1. also please add a short example in the README about migrating from channel-iteration to Next()/Close().

leah: thanks all — i'll post the PR link once ready and ping sampleapps folks for an example update. :rocket:
